problem: Video-LLM VLN agents trained with next-action prediction suffer 'State Drift' on long instructions: they lose track of which sub-goals are done (progress drift) and forget visited landmarks (memory drift), leading to wandering and skipped maneuvers.
motivation: Next-action supervision only enforces locally correct moves and lets the agent guess from shallow cues, with no constraint on internal state. Long-horizon, compositional instructions exacerbate the decoupling of internal state from the real task state, so explicit state regularization is needed.
key_idea: Anchor the Video-LLM's internal state during training with (1) structured text progress descriptions (completed vs remaining sub-goals) generated before each action and (2) a retrospective world model that reconstructs SAM features of the most recently passed landmark from history output tokens.
insight: Both anchors give complementary gains: on the R2R+RxR+EnvDrop setting, IPA alone raises SR 40.8→45.4, MLA alone 40.8→47.7, and both give 49.5; the gain persists at full data (56.9→65.6). Gains grow with trajectory length (SPL relative gain +12.6% short to +33.2% long), consistent with drift being the bottleneck. Auxiliary heads are training-only, so inference cost is unchanged.
method: Progress Annotation Generation: Qwen3-VL annotates GT trajectories, overlaying frame index and action text on frames, with interval sampling, dual-step CoT reasoning, and refinement into a verbatim instruction prefix of completed sub-goals; yields 3.6M samples.

Instruction-Aware Co-training: the ground-truth action is prefixed with the progress description, the prompt adds 'find out which part you have completed', and the model maximizes P(y_prog, a | I, H).

Landmark Frame Mining: Qwen3 decomposes the instruction into atomic sub-goals, Qwen3-VL finds the first appearance frame of each landmark with a strictly increasing time constraint, giving 937k grounded samples with SAM feature maps as targets.

Landmark-Centric World Model: an auxiliary head (linear+LayerNorm projection, learnable H×W spatial queries with cross-attention over LLM output tokens, linear to SAM dim) predicts the SAM feature map of the latest passed landmark frame with an MSE loss.
Two-stage training: Stage 1 uses navigation data plus L_nav + λ_prog L_prog + λ_WM L_WM; Stage 2 adds 240K DAgger rollouts, 400K VideoQA and 230K image-text data, with anchoring losses still active.
StreamVLN backbone: streaming Video-LLM (LLaVA-Video) with history context; the anchoring heads are dropped at deployment.

setting.backbone: StreamVLN with LLaVA-Video Video-LLM (fine-tuned), plus auxiliary SAM-feature decoder head
setting.training_data: R2R, RxR, EnvDrop (180K), ScaleVLN HM3D subset (155K), 3.6M synthesized progress descriptions, 937K grounded landmark SAM samples, 240K DAgger rollouts, 400K VideoQA (LLaVA-Video, ScanQA), 230K MMC4 image-text
setting.observation: monocular RGB streaming video plus instruction
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (move_forward, turn_left, turn_right, stop)
setting.privileged: none at test time (Qwen3-VL annotators only used offline for training data)

numbers.extra: Uses 3.6M progress + 937K landmark data, DAgger, ScaleVLN, generalist VL data
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (comparison on R2R-CE and RxR-CE val unseen), row Ours

numbers.extra: Ablation setting without DAgger, ScaleVLN, or VL data
numbers.evidence: Table ablation, R2R+RxR+EnvDrop columns, both checkmarks

numbers_note: The trajectory-length analysis is only in a figure (no numbers except SPL relative gains +12.6% short and +33.2% long in the text).
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen it reaches SR 65.6 / SPL 62.1, beating StreamVLN (56.9/51.9) and DualVLN (64.3/58.5); NE 4.15 and OSR 69.2 are second to DualVLN. On RxR-CE it reaches SR 61.7 / SPL 53.3 with NE 4.42, above DualVLN (61.4/51.8), and shows real-world Go2 deployment qualitatively.
limitations: Relies on large offline MLLM-generated annotations (Qwen3-VL/Qwen3) that can hallucinate; the progress data still has a 6.04% hallucination rate and 75.6% landmark presence.

Real-world evaluation is only qualitative, with no quantitative success rates; the gain partly depends on large extra data (3.6M+937K samples), and the ablation at full data does not control sample count.
Only monocular RGB and simulated R2R-CE/RxR-CE are evaluated; the world model target is limited to a single latest landmark.
